quote: Most importantly, GMSCs were capable of immunomodulatory functions, specifically suppressed peripheral blood lymphocyte proliferation, induced expression of a wide panel of immunosuppressive factors including IL-10, IDO, inducible NO synthase (iNOS), and cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2) in response to the inflammatory cytokine, IFN-gamma.
summary: IDO is one of several immunosuppressive factors induced by IFN-gamma in gingiva-derived stem cells that ameliorate mouse colitis; IDO itself was not perturbed.

quote: In IDO knockout mice treated with anti-CTLA-4 antibody, we demonstrate a striking delay in B16 melanoma tumor growth and increased overall survival when compared with wild-type mice.
summary: IDO knockout or inhibition enhances anti-CTLA-4 antitumour immunity in mouse melanoma; no colitis or barrier outcome was measured.

quote: Next, we discuss the paracrine interactions between MSCs and innate [dendritic cells (DC)] and adaptive immune cells (T lymphocytes) with a focus on prostaglandin E(2) (PGE(2)), indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO), and toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling pathways.
summary: Review of mesenchymal stem cell immunomodulation and homing that discusses IDO as one mediator; no new data or UC-specific findings.

quote: The loss of T(H)17/T(reg) balance is associated with induction of indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1) by myeloid antigen-presenting dendritic cells and with increased plasma concentration of microbial products.
summary: In HIV patients, IDO1 induction in dendritic cells is associated with a shift from Th17 to Treg cells; not a UC or IBD setting.

quote: Small-molecule inhibitors of IDO exhibit anticancer activity and cooperate with immunotherapy, radiotherapy or chemotherapy to trigger rapid regression of aggressive tumors otherwise resistant to treatment.
summary: Perspective on IDO as a driver of pathogenic inflammation and immune escape in cancer and a target for inhibitors; no colitis data.

quote: Targeting IDO1 represents a therapeutic opportunity in cancer immunotherapy beyond checkpoint blockade or adoptive transfer of chimeric antigen receptor T cells.
summary: Review of IDO1 pathway function and inhibitor development in cancer; no UC-specific content.

quote: More importantly, the dual effect on immune reactions was also observed in human MSCs, in which indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) acts as a switch.
summary: IDO is mentioned as the switch for dual immune effects of human mesenchymal stem cells, with the main experiments on iNOS in mouse MSCs; no colitis data.

quote: Epacadostat is a potent and highly selective IDO1 enzyme inhibitor.
summary: Phase I trial of the IDO1 inhibitor epacadostat with pembrolizumab in advanced solid tumours showed tolerability and antitumour responses; no UC or colitis outcome.

quote: The persistent IDO degradation blocks tryptophan (Trp)-catabolism program and promotes the activation of effector T cells.
summary: A nano-PROTAC degrading IDO boosts antitumour T-cell immunity in mice; the work is in cancer with no colitis outcome.

quote: Mechanistically, we identified that Lactobacillus-derived reactive oxygen species may suppress host kynurenine metabolism, by inhibiting the expression of the metabolizing enzyme, IDO1, in the intestine.
summary: In a stress-induced despair mouse model, Lactobacillus lowers intestinal IDO1 expression and kynurenine; it concerns behaviour, not colitis.

quote: Finally, in vivo IDO blockade affected the development of Tregs specific for orally administered antigens, impaired oral tolerance induction and exacerbated colitis.
summary: IDO expressed by gut CD103+ dendritic cells supports Treg conversion, and IDO inhibition or deletion increased Th1 and Th17 responses and exacerbated colitis in mice.

quote: Mechanistically, ICA inhibited indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO1) expression, therefore suppressing kynurenine (Kyn) production in tumours.
summary: A bacterial metabolite lowers IDO1 expression and Treg differentiation to improve anti-PD1 efficacy in colorectal cancer models; no colitis outcome for IDO1.

quote: Strategies focusing on enhancing Treg function find importance in cytokines TGF-β, IDO, interleukins 10, 27, and 35, and ligands Jagged-1 and OX40L.
summary: Review of Tregs in multiple sclerosis and myasthenia gravis that lists IDO among factors for enhancing Treg function; nothing specific.

quote: Epacadostat was generally well tolerated, effectively normalized kynurenine levels, and produced maximal inhibition of IDO1 activity at doses of ≥100 mg BID.
summary: First-in-human trial shows the IDO1 inhibitor epacadostat is tolerated and lowers plasma kynurenine in cancer patients; no colitis outcome.

quote: We further show that Lys induces the immune tolerance ability of dendritic cells (DCs) by enhancing Trp catabolism towards the kynurenine (Kyn) pathway through activation of the metabolic enzyme indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1) in an aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR)-dependent manner.
summary: A commensal bacterium protects mice from DSS colitis through an AhR-IDO1-kynurenine circuit in dendritic cells that promotes Treg-mediated tolerance, suggesting IDO1 is protective.

quote: Indeed, IDO1 is now considered as an authentic immune regulator not only in pregnancy, but also in autoimmune diseases, chronic inflammation, and tumor immunity.
summary: Up-to-date review of IDO1 structure, enzymatic and non-enzymatic immunoregulatory functions; no UC-specific new data.

quote: The first catabolic step in KP is primarily controlled by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) and tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase (TDO).
summary: Review of kynurenine pathway enzymes including IDO in cardiovascular disease; unrelated to UC.

quote: Reciprocally, Ri. markedly restrained the limit-step enzyme responsible for kynurenine (indoleamine2,3-dioxygenase 1, IDO1) and quinolinic acid (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid 3,4-dioxygenase, 3HAO) generation, thereby decreased Kyn and Quin levels.
summary: Roseburia intestinalis treatment lowered IDO1 expression and kynurenine in depressed mice; this is a depression model, not colitis.

quote: Protection was associated with a reduction of inflammatory scores and colonic expression of pro-inflammatory genes, while a high local expression of the immunoregulatory enzyme indolamine 2, 3 dioxgenase (IDO) was observed.
summary: Probiotic-treated dendritic cells protected mice from TNBS colitis, and protection was accompanied by high colonic IDO expression; IDO function was not tested.

quote: While CTLA-4 and PD-1 are the most-extensively researched targets, results from pre-clinical studies and clinical trials indicate that novel agents, specific for checkpoints such as A2AR, LAG-3, IDO and others, may further contribute to the improvement of patient outcomes, most likely in combinations with anti-CTLA-4 or anti-PD-1 blockade.
summary: Melanoma checkpoint combination review that names IDO only as one emerging target among several.

quote: The contribution of gut bacterial metabolites in the human immune signaling pathway of non-communicable diseases.
summary: Review of gut bacterial metabolites in non-communicable diseases; IDO appears only in the abbreviation list.

quote: We observed associations of genomewide significance between asthma and the following single-nucleotide polymorphisms: rs3771166 on chromosome 2, implicating IL1RL1/IL18R1 (P=3×10(−9)); rs9273349 on chromosome 6, implicating HLA-DQ (P=7×10(−14)); rs1342326 on chromosome 9, flanking IL33 (P=9×10(−10)); rs744910 on chromosome 15 in SMAD3 (P=4×10(−9)); and rs2284033 on chromosome 22 in IL2RB (P=1.1×10(−8)).
summary: Asthma GWAS found a genome-wide significant SNP flanking IL33 (rs1342326); this is an asthma association with no stated direction and no UC data.

quote: Together, our results indicate that, unlike inducible cytokines, IL-33 is constitutively expressed in normal human tissues.
summary: IL-33 is constitutively expressed in the nucleus of endothelial and epithelial cells across normal human tissues, suggesting an alarmin role; not specific to UC.

quote: Accordingly, in situ hybridization demonstrated that endothelial cells constitute a major source of IL-33 mRNA in chronically inflamed tissues from patients with rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn's disease.
summary: IL-33 mRNA is mainly made by endothelial cells in inflamed tissue from Crohn's disease and rheumatoid arthritis patients, and IL-33 is a chromatin-bound nuclear factor.

quote: Here, we investigated the possibility that IL-33 activity may be regulated by proteases released during inflammation.
summary: Neutrophil elastase and cathepsin G cleave IL-33 into mature forms with about tenfold higher activity in cellular assays; UC is mentioned only as a linked disease.
